for a in ./*.flac ; do
 if [[ -f "$a" ]]; then
 if ffmpeg -i "$a" -b:a 320k "${a[@]/%flac/mp3}" >/dev/null 2>&1 ; then
 rm "$a"
 fi
 fi
done

Probably not on headphones, but you'll kick yourself later for not keeping the source when you're listening to that on a big system. Just check the output on even a digital equalizer of that high-bitrate mp3 versus the flac. You'll see the highs and lows are practically gone. That's one of the ways mp3 manages to crunch the file so small: it eliminates the bands that "don't matter," either because people largely don't care or because most people don't have the audio equipment to pick it up.

High-bitrate is a good compromise, but you're still throwing away a lot of hard data in the flac that you can never get back. As long as you're comfortable with that, then carry on... just be aware of it.
